messages:
Asha: starting handoff from EU night -> US day. I'm primary until 14:00 UTC, Kai is secondary. Quick status: no active incidents, but fringe latency alert last night (see runbook link).
Matt: thanks — is there any ongoing mitigation for the kvcache warmup noise?
Asha: we left the cache size relaxed; the autoscaler kicked but latency bins were ok. I left a note in the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-warmup. Follow the 'gradual-scale' steps if it pops again.
Kai: noted. Are we okay with coverage from 06:00-09:00 UTC when spike windows normally hit? I have a meeting 07:30-08:00 and can be reachable but might be delayed.
Asha: good point — Matt can act as interim-primary if you need a short swap. We should document the swap in this thread and update oncall roster.
Matt: I can cover 07:25-08:10. Leave a short comment in the rota.
Sana: quick reminder on paging thresholds: severity is tied to customer impact. Use the incident-bot triage scores but override if multiple customers are degraded. Pager step: P0 -> page escalation lead + infra lead; P1 -> page primary + secondary then wait 5m before escalation.
oncall-bot: incident-bot: alert created (id=INC-20260315-418). score=7.2, metric=frontend_p50_latency, region=eu-west-1.
Asha: that's the alert I saw at 02:14 UTC; it recovered after cache warmed. No customer-visible errors reported in the dashboard. I set the incident status to "monitoring" and added the kvcache note.
Matt: If we see error rate >0.5% for two consecutive 1m windows, escalate to P1 and page the secondary immediately. If >2% or broad customer 5xx, go P0 and activate escalation chain.
Kai: where are the phone numbers for escalation leads? I couldn't find them in the standard runbook (only PD escalation).
Asha: added in the team-runbook contacts section — short list: Maria (infra lead) +1-555-0112, Ken (SRE on-call lead) +1-555-0133. Also: PagerDuty escalation schedule is authoritative. Link: https://redwood.ops/pagerduty-schedule
Sana: procedural note: when paging, include concise context in the message: "what happened", "impact (customers/regions)", "current mitigation", and "ask". Example: "P1: frontend latency spike eu-west-1, ~30% increased p50, no 5xx. Disabled autoscaler bump at 02:16 UTC; request SRE to verify node pool health"
Matt: for handoff checklist before leaving: (1) confirm active alerts acked, (2) update incident channel with known mitigations, (3) set oncall status in rota, (4) confirm secondary contact and lateness windows.
Asha: done — I acked the alert and linked the mitigation. Rota updated. Kai — I'll DM you the brief in case you need to swap.
Kai: thanks. One more: for cross-region fallback, do we prefer model-swap or region-routing for low-latency apps? That affects escalation targets (model infra vs routing infra).
Sana: default is routing fallbacks only for transient capacity. If degraded model quality or quantization faults, escalate to model-oncall. Put that in the incident severity note.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: there is a scheduled model roll tomorrow at 03:00 UTC for the eu cluster — watch for post-deploy latencies; set a temporary heightened watch window 03:00-04:30 UTC if you're primary.
Asha: noted, will keep a close eye and leave a pre-deploy checklist item for whoever's primary at that hour.
Matt: tiny config snippet for pager message (put in the incident chat window):
```
PAGER MESSAGE: P1 | service=frontend | region=eu-west-1 | symptom=latency spike | impact=partial-customer-degradation | mitigation=cache throttle applied | ask=investigate node saturation
```
Kai: perfect. If I need to escalate after 5m with no update, I will page Ken and Maria and mention "escalation after 5m no response".
Sana: also remember to log customer-visible checks: run the synthetic job group: `synth/checkout-flow` and report pass/fail in the thread. If synthetic fails, increase severity one tier.
Asha: I ran `synth/checkout-flow` at 02:40 UTC — passed from eu-west-1. Kept the results in the incident note.
Matt: final: if we ever need an all-hands paging (major outage), use the "page-all" escalation but coordinate with SRE lead first (Ken). It's a high-noise action.
Kai: acknowledged. I'll leave a short follow-up in #incidents if anything changes during my 07:30 meeting.
Asha: wrap up: handoff complete. Primary=Asha until 14:00 UTC, secondary=Kai, fallback=Matt. Handoff checklist items: runbook links posted, pending deploy watched, contact numbers added.
Matt: thanks — good handoff. :thumbsup:
